draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Mysore Palace! After the old palace burned down, this one was built from 1897 to 1912, and on show nights it lights up with 100,000 bulbs.
draft.hungryLine: Wander over to Devaraja Market for fresh fruit, spices and piles of colourful kumkum.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Mysore Palace is a 3 minute walk, Jaganmohan Palace is 10 minutes away, and Devaraja Market is about 12 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet corner in the Jaganmohan Palace art gallery, full of Raja Ravi Varma paintings.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Devaraja Market was built in 1886 right over the Dewan Poornaiah Canal, which supplied drinking water to the palace.

spots.name: Mysore Palace
spots.detail: 3 min walk · Rosewood doors, ivory inlay and royal portraits

spots.name: Jaganmohan Palace
spots.detail: 10 min walk · Royal mansion turned art gallery

spots.name: Devaraja Market
spots.detail: 12 min walk · Flowers, spices and sandalwood since 1886

legends.title: Chamundi's sister
legends.body: Legend says each drop of the demon Mahisasura's blood would create a new demon. So Chamundi asked Tripura Sundari for help, and she drank every drop before it touched the ground.

tips.title: Stay for the evening lights.
tips.body: The light and sound show starts at 7PM, and the whole palace lights up at the end.

tips.title: Be ready to leave your shoes.
tips.body: You have to take your shoes off before going into the palace.

story.title: The Wadiyars' capital
story.body: The Kingdom of Mysore was founded around 1399, and the city stayed its capital for almost six centuries.

story.title: The first palace
story.body: The first palace on this spot was built under Kanthirava Narasaraja I, then destroyed and rebuilt several times.

story.title: Hyder Ali and Tipu
story.body: The kingdom became a sultanate under Hyder Ali and Tipu, before turning into a princely state under the British.

story.title: Fire and a new start
story.body: After the old palace burned down, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV commissioned a new one, designed by Henry Irwin.

story.title: The palace today
story.body: The Indo-Saracenic palace was finished in 1912, and the Mysore Dasara festival is held on its grounds every year.
